title: Nonderogatory Operators: Module-Theoretic Extension to Infinite Dimensions
description: Extends the cyclic vector theory from finite-dimensional matrices to general endomorphisms on K-modules using the evaluation map p -> p(T)(v). Establishes the module-theoretic framework where 'nonderogatory' means 'V is a cyclic K[X]-module' -- the correct generalization to infinite dimensions where no characteristic polynomial exists.

overview.historicalContext: The passage from matrix theory to module theory for linear operators was pioneered by Emmy Noether and her school in the 1920s-30s. The key insight is that a vector space V with an endomorphism T becomes a K[X]-module via the action X . v = T(v). The rational canonical form (invariant factor decomposition) then becomes the structure theorem for finitely generated torsion modules over the PID K[X]. For infinite-dimensional spaces, this framework extends naturally: V as a K[X]-module may have countably many invariant factors, and the 'nonderogatory' condition becomes 'V is a cyclic K[X]-module.' This formalization makes the module-theoretic framework explicit in Lean 4, providing the correct dimension-free generalization.
overview.problemStatement: Establish the module-theoretic framework for cyclic vectors and nonderogatory endomorphisms that works in any dimension. Define the evaluation map, prove it bridges polynomial algebra and cyclic subspaces, and connect to the finite-dimensional matrix theory.
overview.proofStrategy: Define the evaluation map phi_v : K[X] -> V, p -> p(T)(v). Show it is K-linear with image = cyclic subspace of v and kernel = annihilator ideal of v. Then 'v is cyclic' is equivalent to phi_v being surjective. The minimal polynomial of T lies in the kernel (annihilator), and the annihilator is closed under polynomial multiplication (making it a K[X]-ideal). This gives a clean, dimension-free characterization: nonderogatory = cyclic K[X]-module = evaluation map surjective for some v.
keyInsights: The evaluation map phi_v : K[X] -> V is the fundamental bridge between algebra (polynomials) and geometry (cyclic subspaces). Its surjectivity characterizes cyclic vectors.
In infinite dimensions, 'nonderogatory' must be reformulated: there is no characteristic polynomial, so the correct definition is 'V is a cyclic K[X]-module.'
The annihilator of v (polynomials p with p(T)v = 0) is an ideal of K[X], not just a K-subspace. This is the module-theoretic upgrade of the annihilator concept.
The cyclic subspace is automatically T-invariant: T maps span{T^k v} into itself. This follows from T^(k+1)v being in the generating set.
For finite-dimensional V, the module-theoretic and matrix-theoretic notions coincide via the structure theorem for f.g. modules over PIDs.
prerequisites: K[X]-module structure on vector spaces via endomorphisms
Minimal polynomials and their annihilation property
Structure theorem for finitely generated modules over PIDs (for the connection to invariant factors)

sections.title: Core Definitions
sections.summary: Defines cyclicSubspace (span of T-orbit), IsCyclicVector (orbit = V), and IsNonderogatory (cyclic K[X]-module = existence of cyclic vector).
sections.mathContext: The cyclic subspace $W_v = \text{span}_K\{v, Tv, T^2v, \ldots\}$ is the smallest $T$-invariant subspace containing $v$. A cyclic vector generates all of $V$. In the module picture, $W_v$ is the $K[X]$-submodule generated by $v$.

sections.title: The Evaluation Map
sections.summary: Defines evalMap T v : K[X] ->_K V sending p to p(T)(v). Proves K-linearity using AlgHom.toLinearMap. Proves basic computation rules: evalMap(1) = v, evalMap(X) = Tv, evalMap(X^k) = T^k v.
sections.mathContext: The evaluation map $\varphi_v : K[X] \to V$, $p \mapsto p(T)v$ is $K$-linear because $\text{aeval}_T$ is a $K$-algebra homomorphism and evaluation at $v$ is $K$-linear. Its image is the cyclic subspace and its kernel is the annihilator ideal.

sections.title: Cyclic Subspace Properties
sections.summary: Proves v and T^k v are in the cyclic subspace, and that the cyclic subspace is T-invariant (T maps it into itself).
sections.mathContext: $T^0 v = v \in W_v$ and $T^k v \in W_v$ by definition. $T$-invariance: $T(T^k v) = T^{k+1}v \in W_v$, and $W_v$ is a $K$-span, so $T$ maps the span into itself.

sections.title: Image = Cyclic Subspace
sections.summary: Proves range(evalMap T v) = cyclicSubspace T v. Forward: by polynomial induction, p(T)v is in span{T^k v}. Backward: by span induction, elements of span{T^k v} are in the image.
sections.mathContext: Every $p(T)v = \sum a_k T^k v$ is in $W_v$ (monomial-by-monomial). Conversely, $T^k v = (X^k)(T)v = \varphi_v(X^k) \in \text{Im}(\varphi_v)$, and the image is a submodule.

sections.title: Cyclic Vector Characterization
sections.summary: Two characterizations: v is cyclic iff evalMap is surjective, and v is cyclic iff every w = p(T)v for some polynomial p.
sections.mathContext: $v$ cyclic $\iff W_v = V \iff \text{Im}(\varphi_v) = V \iff \varphi_v$ surjective $\iff \forall w \in V, \exists p \in K[X], p(T)v = w$.

sections.title: Annihilator Properties
sections.summary: Proves the minimal polynomial kills every vector, the annihilator is closed under multiplication (ideal structure), and multiples of minpoly annihilate v.
sections.mathContext: The annihilator $\text{Ann}(v) = \{p \in K[X] : p(T)v = 0\}$ is an ideal: if $p(T)v = 0$ then $(qp)(T)v = q(T)(p(T)v) = 0$. Since $K[X]$ is a PID, $\text{Ann}(v) = (\mu_v)$ for a unique monic polynomial $\mu_v$ dividing $\mu_T$.

sections.title: Finite-Dimensional Connection
sections.summary: States the bridge to finite-dimensional matrix theory: defines IsCyclicVectorMatrix and IsNonderogatoryMatrix matching the OQ05OQ01 definitions, and states that matrix nonderogatory implies module nonderogatory.
sections.mathContext: In finite dimensions, $M$ nonderogatory ($\mu_M = \chi_M$) $\iff$ $K^n$ is a cyclic $K[X]$-module $\iff$ $M$ has a cyclic vector. The forward direction is proved in OQ05OQ01 via union avoidance.

sections.title: Structure Theorem Connection
sections.summary: States the structure theorem characterization: nonderogatory iff no nonzero polynomial of degree < deg(minpoly) annihilates T. This connects to the invariant factor decomposition.
sections.mathContext: The structure theorem for f.g. modules over $K[X]$ gives $V \cong \bigoplus_i K[X]/(f_i)$. The module is cyclic $\iff$ there is a single factor. The characterization via polynomial non-annihilation is the algebraic dual of cyclicity.

conclusion.summary: Module-theoretic framework for cyclic vectors and nonderogatory endomorphisms, valid in all dimensions. 12 theorems/lemmas with 3 sorries (orbit dimension bound, finite-dim bridge, structure theorem characterization) and 0 axioms.
conclusion.implications: Provides the correct infinite-dimensional generalization: 'nonderogatory' = 'cyclic K[X]-module', independent of characteristic polynomials. The evaluation map is the central construction bridging polynomial algebra and cyclic subspaces.
openQuestions: Prove the orbit dimension bound: for integral T, T^k v is expressible via lower powers for k >= deg(minpoly)
Formalize the full structure theorem for f.g. modules over PIDs in Lean 4
For countably generated torsion K[X]-modules, prove countable union avoidance over uncountable fields to construct cyclic vectors explicitly
